newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says Egyptian peace effort nearly dead.
newsitem.headline: PLO says Egyptian peace effort nearly dead.

text.p: A senior aide to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Wednesday Egyptian efforts to revive Israeli-PLO peace talks were near collapse and complained that Washington had withdrawn from peacemaking.

Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, secretary-general of the Palestinian Authority, blamed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the failure of an Egyptian mediation drive and warned that the West Bank and Gaza were on the verge of an explosion.
He spoke as a new wave of violence rocked the Palestinian territories. Israeli soldiers shot dead a Palestinian in a clash in Gaza and wounded at least 26 in the West Bank town of Hebron.
"Mr Netanyahu has dealt with the Egyptian moves as a public relations game and not with the appropriate seriousness," Abdel-Rahman told a news conference in PLO-ruled al-Bireh.
"I can almost say that this move has ended."

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, eager to revive Israeli-PLO peace talks frozen since Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March, dispatched his advisor Osama al-Baz on several shuttle missions between Arafat and Netanyahu with no apparent success.
The PLO demands an Israeli halt to settlement activities for talks to resume. Netanyahu rejects the demand and wants Arafat to restore security ties with Israel and to crack down on militants.
Egypt stepped in as the main mediator between the Palestinians and Israelis over the past few weeks after a bid by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross to defuse the crisis failed.
Mubarak said on Tuesday Egypt would not resume its negotiating efforts for the time being but that contacts between the two sides would produce progress soon.

"I think over the past two weeks there have been some contacts between the Palestinians and Israel but I am not in a position to reveal any of that," Mubarak said. "Let them work. I hope they can conclude something within one week, 10 days."
Abdel-Rahman said Mubarak's comments clearly meant "that he was returning the ball to the Israeli court".
"I can say that after three weeks of no movement it means that Egypt has grown convinced that Israel was not serious about peace," Abdel-Rahman said.
He complained that Middle East peacemaking was not on the top of U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's agenda.
"It is very clear that there is an American withdrawal from its role from the peace process in the Middle East," Abdel-Rahman said.
"Mrs Albright thinks that the Middle East is not the first priority for the American administration. She is more European than Mediterranean," he said.
Abdel-Rahman warned that Palestinians were growing more frustrated and losing faith in the peace process.
"Honestly, the situation is on the verge of an explosion," Abdel-Rahman said.
